place.source_title: United States Post Office, Ohio Avenue and North Street

brief: Classical Revival federal post office of 1915 on a corner: one tall storey over a raised basement, red brick with limestone trim, a row of round-arched windows set in stone surrounds, a central entrance up a flight of steps, a stone name frieze and a flagpole at the corner. Blue collection boxes by the steps.

facade.notes: the Sidney OH post office (1915): one tall storey of red brick with limestone pilasters, three big round-arched openings (the centre one the door) between rectangular windows, a raised basement with steps and railings, an inscribed parapet; globe lamps, meters, newspaper boxes

why.note: a civic building is a raised, symmetric block set apart by steps, lawn and a portico: the public building as a temple
the Public Buildings Act era: Treasury-designed classical post offices in county seats
